subject: Maths
central_question: How can we recognise, represent, extend, and explain patterns in numbers and shapes?
in_scope_units: 1.1 What is Mathematics? — patterns and explanations in everyday life and science
1.2 Patterns in Numbers — whole-number sequences and number theory
1.3 Visualising Number Sequences — dot and block representations
1.4 Relations among Number Sequences — links among odd, square, triangular, hexagonal, cube, and power sequences
1.5 Patterns in Shapes — regular polygons, complete graphs, stacked shapes, and Koch snowflakes
1.6 Relation to Number Sequences — counting features in changing shapes

known_pitfalls.claim: Guessing the next term completely explains a pattern.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter also requires a rule and an explanation of why it works.

known_pitfalls.claim: Adding consecutive odd numbers gives triangular numbers.
known_pitfalls.correction: Starting with 1, their successive sums give square numbers.

recommended_example_progression: Extend the sequences in Section 1.2 Table 1.
Use Section 1.3 Table 2 to visualise triangular, square, and cube numbers.
Use Section 1.4 to connect sums of odd numbers with squares.
Use Section 1.4 to add consecutive triangular numbers.
Use Sections 1.5–1.6 to count features in shape sequences.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use the Figure it Out and Math Talk tasks across Sections 1.1–1.6 and the chapter Summary on page 12.
